# Nebula theme for DeepSeek Harness

A client theme bundle for the DeepSeek Harness web UI: a filamented indigo-plum
night sky with a liv

e fire field along the bottom edge. The fire stays a low
ember line while the harness is idle and ri

ses into separate flame fronts while
any agent is thinking. The sky itself never brightens.
*A fresh chat with the sidebar collapsed: idle embers under the drifting sky.*
*Idle — a low ember line under a still, drifting sky.*
*Thinking — the flame fronts rise and the floating chats pick up the ember frame.*

The idle and thinking images are rendered from `demo/index.html`
with synthetic content; no real ses

sion data is used. The first image is the live
client with the sidebar collapsed.
## What it does

- **Sky** — one generated texture (domain-warped fBm, dark dust lanes, a crimson
underglow) that is

drawn once, dithered against banding, and then left alone.
It drifts slowly and never reacts to agen

t state.
- **Depth** — a second, larger copy of the sky drifts the other way and breathes
gently, so

the cloud structure shifts against itself instead of sliding as one
flat image.
- **Fire** — a 256×

112 flame field with per-cell cooling, wind that leans with
height, and bilinear advection. Idle run

s it at 12 fps as a short ember line;
thinking runs it at 30 fps and raises the source. A 48×20 down

sample of the
same field is blurred into the sky as firelight.
- **Readability** — a dark reading ve

il sits above the flames and below the UI,
so transcript text keeps its contrast. The composer becom

es a glass slab so
the flame base glows through it.
- **Palette** — a token layer overrides the acti

ve palette in both light and
dark mode, so the theme keeps its night-sky identity whichever mode is
static warm field instead of animating.

The theme never reads chat content. It asks the Session service only whether
any session is currentl

y running, then projects that onto one body attribute
(`data-ds-nebula-think`).
## Install
Requires a DeepSeek Harness build with the web client (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`).
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Replace `web` with the profile you actually boot. The bundle is a local package
(`@local/nebula-them

e`) and is not published to npm, so install it from the
checkout as shown.
To remove it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
The package is a normal DSH bundle:
| File | Role |

| `package.json` | Declares `dsh.bundle` (this patch) and `dsh.client` (web client module) |
| `cord

is.patch.yml` | Inserts the `nebula-theme` row |
| `index.js` | Host half; intentionally empty |
| `

client.js` | The whole theme: token layer, CSS, sky generator, fire field, status bridge |
| `locale

/*.json` | Theme name and description in eight locales |
| `icon.svg` | Theme icon |
At apply time the client half:

1. registers a palette override through `ctx.theme.overrideTokens`;
2. injects one scoped `<style>`

. appends the parallax layer and the fire/glow canvases to `<body>`;
5. sets the `data-ds-nebula-the
enever any session is running.

Every effect returns a disposer, so disabling the plugin removes the style,
the canvases, the textur
e URL, and the attributes without touching the app.
## Develop

There is no build step and no runtime dependency beyond React (provided by the
host).
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The capture script drives headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol because
virtual-time capture do

es not advance `requestAnimationFrame`, which the fire
needs in order to ramp. It uses synthetic con

ance `requestAnimationFrame`, which the fire
needs in order to ramp. It uses synthetic content only.

`demo/index.html` runs the real `client.js` against a minimal
module-loader stub and a mock shell, s

o it doubles as a quick visual check. Add
`?thinking=1` to see the thinking state.
## Compatibility

Built and tested against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.x`. It relies on the public
client seams `ctx.theme.o

verrideTokens`, `ctx.slots`, and the
`shell.overlay` slot; it does not patch host files.

The floating-chats styling is optional. If the `@local/active-chats` plugin is
installed it picks up

the space-glass frame and the ember thinking glow; if it
is not, those rules never match.
